qt: to the Commission Matjaž Nemec (S&D), Mounir Satouri (Verts/ALE), Margrete Auken (Verts/ALE), Nora Mebarek (S&D), Pierre Larrouturou (S&D), Ivan Vilibor Sinčić (NI), Francisco Guerreiro (Verts/ALE), Chris MacManus (The Left), Evin Incir (S&D), Irena Joveva (Renew), Sylvie Guillaume (S&D) Subject:

In its conclusions on the review of ongoing financial assistance to Palestine, the Commission has recommended to ‘extend the screening of PEGASE Civil Servants and Pensioners and Cash Transfer Programme to 1st degree relative of beneficiaries, excluding minors, to be agreed with the Palestinian Authority’.1 To date, PEGASE already includes checks on indirect beneficiaries, as the screening system takes into consideration the lists of detainees, families of perpetrators of terrorist attacks and security staff. 1.

How does extending the screening process to all first-degree relatives of beneficiaries fall in line with EU guidelines and with the jurisprudence of the Court of Justice of the EU, in particular the judgment of the General Court in Case T-212/22 ‘PrigozhinavCouncil’?2
What is the evidential trigger and legal basis for such an extensive screening process, and what legal remedies will be available for the affected individuals?
How will the Commission ensure that such an extension does not disproportionally affect the most vulnerable groups, specifically women, people with disabilities and the elderly?3

As stated in the conclusions on the review, in April 2023, of the 106 596 Palestinian families that benefited from social allowances, 91 261 were extremely poor, 41 266 were female-headed, 16 395 were headed by a person with a disability and 42 130 by an elderly person.
at: (English version) to the Commission Matjaž Nemec (S&D), Mounir Satouri (Verts/ALE), Margrete Auken (Verts/ALE), Nora Mebarek (S&D), Pierre Larrouturou (S&D), Ivan Vilibor Sinčić (NI), Francisco Guerreiro (Verts/ALE), Chris MacManus (The Left), Evin Incir (S&D), Irena Joveva (Renew), Sylvie Guillaume (S&D) (9 January 2024) Subject: Commission conclusions on the review of EU financial assistance to Palestine — extended screening of PEGASE In its conclusions on the review of ongoing financial assistance to Palestine, the Commission has recommended to ‘extend the screening of PEGASE Civil Servants and Pensioners and Cash Transfer Programme to 1st degree relative of beneficiaries, excluding minors, to be agreed with the Palestinian Authority’. (1) To date, PEGASE already includes checks on indirect beneficiaries, as the screening system takes into consideration the lists of detainees, families of perpetrators of terrorist attacks and security staff. 1. How does extending the screening process to all first-degree relatives of beneficiaries fall in line with EU guidelines and with the jurisprudence of the Court of Justice of the EU, in particular the judgment of the General Court in Case T-212/22 ‘PrigozhinavCouncil’? (2) 2. What is the evidential trigger and legal basis for such an extensive screening process, and what legal remedies will be available for the affected individuals? 3. How will the Commission ensure that such an extension does not disproportionally affect the most vulnerable groups, specifically women, people with disabilities and the elderly? (3) (10 April 2024) The review of the EU ongoing financial assistance for Palestine (4) was carried out following the terrorist attacks by Hamas against Israel on 7 October 2023 (5). The Commission is responsible to ensure the correct implementation of the EU external funding, in accordance with the principle of sound financial management. Whereas the Commission has a system of safeguards in place, the Financial Regulation (e.g., Article 74 (2)) (6) specifies the duties of the authorising officer who is responsible to put in place the requisite internal control systems. Given the situation on the ground, the context of unforeseen important developments, and to avoid any risk of aid diversion, the Commission has an obligation to pursue extra vigilance in the implementation of the EU external funding, also with a view to due diligence, precautionary principles, political and reputational risks. The action related to the extension of the screening of the Mécanisme Palestino-européen de Gestion de l’Aide Socioéconomique (PEGASE) civil servants and pensioners, and cash transfer programme to first-degree relative of beneficiaries (action 2), has been proposed in line with these obligations. It will be implemented, following discussions with the Palestinian Authority, in line with the relevant legal provisions, including the principle of proportionality. The review explicitly excludes minors from the scope of the action.

As stated in the conclusions on the review, in April 2023, of the 106 596 Palestinian families that benefited from social allowances, 91 261 were extremely poor, 41 266 were female-headed, 16 395 were headed by a person with a disability and 42 130 by an elderly person. This designation shall not be construed as recognition of a State of Palestine and is without prejudice to the individual positions of the Member States on this issue.
